title: Span, Memory and Performance
summary: Writing fast C# without unsafe code - value types and the stack, Span<T> and ReadOnlySpan<T> as views over arrays and strings, slicing without copying, stackalloc, ArrayPool for reusing buffers, ref struct rules, and measuring before optimising.

cards.a:
No: it is a view over the same array

A span is a pointer and a length over existing memory. Nothing is copied, so `span[0] = 9` changes `numbers[1]`.

cards.q: Why can a `Span<T>` not be a field of a class?
cards.a:
It may point into a stack frame that the object outlives

`Span<T>` is a `ref struct`, allowed only on the stack, so it can never dangle. Store a `Memory<T>` in a field instead.

cards.q: Which avoids creating new strings while splitting "a,b,c"?
cards.a:
slicing line.AsSpan() at each comma

Spans view the original characters; Split and Substring create new strings.
